name: Celery
covers: Rerail's own Celery rules, from the Celery docs and maintainers' review advice, for idempotent, serializable tasks dispatched after commit.

rules.title: Celery practice: a task delayed past the broker's visibility timeout
Celery practice: a task sent between a SQLAlchemy write and its commit
Celery practice: Celery set to send or accept pickle messages

caught.text:
from celery import Celery

app = Celery("proj", broker="redis://localhost:6379/0")
app.conf.update(
    task_serializer="pickle",
    result_serializer="pickle",
    accept_content=["json", "pickle"],
)

passes.text:
from celery import Celery

app = Celery("proj", broker="redis://localhost:6379/0")
app.conf.update(
    task_serializer="json",
    result_serializer="json",
    accept_content=["json"],
)

rules.title: Celery practice: a task waits on another task's result
Celery practice: a SQLAlchemy model or session, a set, a file, a lambda or a function passed as a Celery task argument
Celery practice: task named by a string that no task of the run registers
